11	When adopting Prettier repo-wide (SYS-598) surfaced a conflict — CLAUDE.md mandated that all `@mantine/*` imports stay multi-line/one-specifier-per-line, but Prettier has no per-package import formatting concept and collapsed them to one line — the first instinct was to write a local ESLint autofix rule (mirroring the existing `local/require-use-client` pattern) to re-expand them after every Prettier run.
12	
13	The user rejected this: "I think it would be simpler to drop the Mantine-specific rule and just let Prettier format the imports like any other."
14	
15	**Why:** A custom rule fighting Prettier's own output is exactly the kind of "bespoke or idiosyncratic style" this project's SYS-598 ticket was trying to eliminate. Two tools each trying to own import formatting is fragile (order-dependent: prettier collapses, eslint --fix re-expands) and adds maintenance surface for a convention that wasn't load-bearing — it existed only to keep Mantine import diffs clean, a nice-to-have, not a correctness requirement like [[project_claim_page_no_home_link]]-style invariants.
16	
17	**How to apply:** When a hand-written formatting convention conflicts with Prettier's actual output, default to relaxing the convention to match plain Prettier rather than building tooling to preserve the exception — unless the convention encodes a real invariant (e.g. `local/require-use-client`, which prevents a genuine RSC bug, not just a style preference). Ask before investing in a custom autofix rule for a cosmetic-only rule.

- Wrote a one-off TypeScript-compiler-API codemod to split all 40 files / 55 flagged imports it caught into separate statements, then ran `eslint --fix` (simple-import-sort resorted everything) and `npm run format` to normalize.
